title: What If Jupiter's Great Red Spot Kept Shrinking?

scenes.text: What if Jupiter's Great Red Spot kept shrinking? It once fit three Earths side by side.
In the late 1800s it spanned about 41,000 kilometers across.
When Voyager flew by in 1979, it measured about 23,000 kilometers.
Hubble later measured just under 16,500 kilometers, the smallest ever recorded.
Yet NASA says its winds haven't weakened, and the storm is growing taller and darker as it shrinks.
Winds on its edge even sped up by 8 percent from 2009 to 2020. Scientists still don't know why.

description:
What if Jupiter's Great Red Spot kept shrinking?
